layers.realDetail: About 30 cm in our copy; objects need to be about 1 m across to be recognised
layers.positionAccuracy: Source images agree with each other to better than 3 m (99th percentile) and sit a median 2.1 m from the CTX base map, 95.4% within 6 m (Fergason and others 2020)
caveats: Taken between 2007 and 2017, before the rover landed. Rover tracks and hardware are not in it, and sand may have moved.
Lit by the afternoon Sun at the time of each image. Dark patches can be shadows, not dark ground.
One black-and-white band. It shows brightness, not colour.
layers.title: Ground from orbit
layers.processing: Cut to the site's box and redrawn as map tiles for zoom 12 to 18. One tile pixel at zoom 18 is 0.30 m on the ground. Places with no data are transparent.

layers.positionAccuracy: Source images agree with each other to better than 3 m (99th percentile) and sit a median 2.1 m from the CTX base map, 95.4% within 6 m (Fergason and others 2020)
layers.heightAccuracy: Median 0.4 m below the CTX terrain mosaic it was aligned to (Fergason and others 2020)
caveats: Rocks, ledges and ripples smaller than about 3 to 5 m are not in this model.
Made from images taken between 2007 and 2017, before the rover landed. Sand may have moved since.
Where two source models meet there can be a small step that is not real.
layers.title: Terrain height
layers.processing: Cut to the site's box and stored as height tiles for zoom 11 to 15, to the nearest 0.1 m. One tile pixel at zoom 15 is 2.4 m on the ground, so the 3D view is smoother than the 1 m grid. Past the edge of the box the edge height is repeated so the surface has no cliff; that is not data.
